answer.rationale: Only memory_c2 speaks directly to the one lever that can satisfy an 18% mandate the incumbent has refused to fund, so it is the single memory worth the verification slot. Its stated evidence is narrow in a way that matters here: it records unit cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy  ery reliability, quality yield, or capacity headroom. Those are precisely the dimensions at risk with the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, so I want the original record to see what component, what volume share, and what delivery performance actually sat behind 'onboarding was quick.' memory_c4 (renegotiation recovers margin) is effectively foreclosed \u2014 the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, so benchmarking has no lever left. memory_c5 (defer) is unavailable in substance: the contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, so deferring is not a neutral hold, it is an uncovered supply gap against a line with no buffer. memory_c1 and memory_c6 describe real value in incumbent stability and multi-year volume pricing, but neither closes an 18% gap when price is closed. memory_c3 (second source) is the strongest risk-control precedent and I am borrowing its logic rather than its action: with one decision available, adding a second source leaves the expiring primary unresolved. So I intend to move primary supply to the low-cost vendor, but structured as a phased cutover rather than a clean flip \u2014 qualification lots and a first tranche well under full volume, with dual-running on the constrained items and explicit delivery-performance and yield gates before the remaining volume transfers. The downstream risk I am flagging is that the cost mandate is measured this cycle while delivery and quality degradation would surface later: an 18% unit-cost win booked now can be silently reversed by expedites, scrap, or a missed committed-volume penalty at 94% utilization, and total cost of ownership is the objective, not unit price. I am not treating memory_c2 as evidence of reliability under load, because it does not claim that; if the archived record shows the prior switch was a low-criticality part or a small volume share, this should shrink to a guarded qualification-only step and the primary gap should be bridged by a short bridge extension instead.
